description: Generate a versioned, content-addressed React or Vue file-set artifact, or a self-contained static HTML document with sample data, from a validated UiSchema tree. Select draft, build, or release validation; build is the default blocking gate of static checks (schema, registry, readiness, prop/slot/event/binding contracts, dependency closure and HTML fallbacks; the static gate does not install or run the generated application), and every response includes a validationReceipt naming applied policy, checks, omissions, and evidence disposition. Receipts produced after artifact construction also name that artifact's content hash. Release receipts retain accepted caller-supplied evidence references without claiming independent execution. The artifact includes exact dependencies and required consumer-supplied domain actions. Legacy code/fileExtension/imports aliases remain for compatibility. Accepts schemaRef from design.compose; save it before the 30-minute reference expires. Release receipts report evidenceVerification:file-verified-not-re-executed. Local JSON evidence files are opened and SHA-256, passed status and artifact binding are verified; evidence is not re-executed. contentHash names the evidence file-byte digest. OODS-V162 reports missing files or envelopes; OODS-V163 reports invalid JSON, byte hash, status or artifact binding. Portable React/Vue generation uses an assembly-time readiness attestation bound to shipped package bytes and emits real artifacts without source or test files. Missing or tampered readiness evidence returns OODS-N015 without an artifact. Host repository generation retains direct readiness checks. Application options.theme accepts light, dark and hc, with options.brand in the brand registry (A and B ship), for both the shell and embedded chart assets. Authored Subscription payment histories render through public viz.render; absent payment history produces a named empty state without claiming a rendered series. Both assets remain verbatim in React and Vue. Bound record-array charts support bar, line, area, scatter and heatmap with explicit sampleRows; trait titles, descriptions and units accompany generated static SVG. Invoice bar and Usage line are authored in detail and dashboard layouts. Relationship detail and workflow declare an edge-array force_graph over optional neighborhood rows, explicitly labelled synthetic. Source and target IDs produce sorted distinct nodes and row-ordered directed links; a true bidirectional flag adds the reverse link, with directed-pair deduplication and no invented values or groups. Missing or malformed edge fields fail closed. VizGraphPreview embeds the exact public SVG inside a named wrapper. React/Vue application output is supported. HTML shares its record renderer with repl document output: labelled native form controls, local list search/filter/sort/pagination, keyboard tabs, charts and selectable workflow screens and loading/error/empty/success states. Domain actions display an integration notice and never claim a saved, deleted or navigated record. The build profile statically validates HTML contracts and fallback absence; it does not launch a browser, run axe or measure text parity. HTML opens directly from disk with embedded styles and scripts. Broad HTML browser coverage is recorded separately from generation checks. options.payloadMode file writes every artifact file plus artifact.json beside the saved-schema store (<store>/../payloads/code.generate-<content hash prefix>/) and returns a payload block of file references instead of the artifact, for clients with a result-size cap; a directory that cannot be written is OODS-S020 with no payload. React/Vue substitution uses the mapped package export and translated normalized props for single screens and workflows. Artifact substitutions record mapping identity and exact package versions; install steps name the team dependencies. An explicit mapping version or an installed package manifest is required. Mapped team components receive advisory componentContracts reports from the shared contract scenarios through the generated adapters. With a preview host and an installed Chromium browser (OODS_CONTRACT_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE or OODS_PLAYWRIGHT_WS_ENDPOINT), the host executes real React/Vue checks; it does not download browsers or install team packages. Reports bind package, adapter and contract bytes, enumerate met, unmet and not-checked obligations, and travel in file payloads too. Unavailable checks and the 45-second check budget remain not-checked; unmet obligations add OODS-V218 warnings without refusing generation. Unmeasured obligations remain not checked. options.output application delivers a runnable single-screen React/Vue app with strict TypeScript, package.json, Vite config, index.html and entry, deterministic sample data and a README. For HTML, application output is the same standalone document. The default remains component output for React/Vue; their workflows already emit apps. A generated app installs its @oods packages from npm, at the exact versions the install block names. Domain actions show a visible integration notice until the consumer supplies its handler; no backend change is fabricated. Sample fields use authored examples/defaults/enums or neutral typed values. Missing payment history produces a named empty SVG state, with no chart data or public viz.render call.

artifactContentHash.description: Exact generated artifact hash inspected by this evidence.

contentHash.description: SHA-256 of the local JSON evidence file bytes. The file must contain status: passed and this artifactContentHash.

reference.description: Local JSON evidence file, absolute or relative to the server working directory. Opened during release validation.

inputSchema.description: Generate framework-specific code from a validated UiSchema. A workflow schema generates a runnable React or Vue application with navigation, local store and deterministic sample data.

framework.description: Target framework. HTML uses the same record document renderer as repl render; build checks are static and do not execute a browser.

brand.description: Token brand shared by the generated shell and embedded charts. React/Vue app shells default to A. Unscoped HTML preserves the existing document default brand; an explicit HTML theme without a brand selects A.

output.description: React/Vue: component output by default, or a runnable single-screen application. Workflows emit applications. HTML always emits a standalone static sample document, including when application is requested.

payloadMode.description: inline (default) returns the artifact in the response. file writes every artifact file plus artifact.json beside the saved-schema store (<store>/../payloads/code.generate-<digest>/) and returns a payload block of file references; the artifact is then omitted from the response and code is empty.

styling.description: React/Vue styling strategy: inline style objects, design-token CSS variables, or Tailwind utility classes. HTML uses document CSS; requesting Tailwind reports OODS-N018 as a draft warning or a build/release error.

theme.description: Application and embedded chart theme. Preserves a composed theme unless explicitly overridden; otherwise defaults to light.

typescript.description: When true, emit TypeScript prop types (React) or typed defineProps (Vue). Ignored for HTML.

profile.description: Validation profile. draft reports non-structural target/contract gaps, including workflow-state contract gaps, as warnings; build is the default blocking gate of static checks (schema, registry, readiness, contracts, dependencies, fallbacks; the static gate does not install or run the generated application); release additionally requires six local JSON evidence files with matching SHA-256 contentHash, passed status and artifactContentHash.

releaseEvidence.description: Evidence for release. All six named classes are required by the release gate and must bind to the generated artifact contentHash. The server opens each local JSON reference and checks its SHA-256 against contentHash, its passed status and its artifactContentHash. It does not re-execute the evidence.

schemaRef.description: Reference to a cached UiSchema returned by design.compose.

name: code_generate
